asset.title: Premium wellness recap for black raspberry juice

creativeDirectionOptions.prompt:
Create a cinematic, emotionally engaging 15-second highlight reel for a premium wellness tasting, family gathering, or lifestyle brand moment centered on Berrywell Gold Black Raspberry Juice. This is a physical product recap styled like a modern event film, not a generic product ad.

Use the attached reference image as the source of truth for the product appearance. Preserve the bottle shape, label layout, deep burgundy-black liquid, gold accents, cylindrical carton, and overall premium Korean black raspberry identity. Do not copy the reference image’s exact tabletop scene, background, lighting, props, or composition; create a fresh recap environment around it.

Concept: a polished wellness and gifting moment around a rich black raspberry juice ritual — elegant pouring, family-style serving, clinking glasses, close-ups of berries, and a warm premium atmosphere that feels shareable and socially believable in Singapore.

Visual style:
- cinematic handheld and smooth gimbal blend
- shallow depth of field, natural warm light, soft highlights on glass and label
- premium but believable home dining or boutique wellness setting
- subtle slow motion on pours and reactions
- modern social-media recap editing with clean momentum

15-second structure:

Scene 1 — Opening Atmosphere (0-3s)
- Establish a refined table scene with the Berrywell bottle and carton standing proudly beside fresh black raspberries.
- Show a hand sliding the bottle into frame, soft sunlight, glass reflections, and a calm premium mood.
- Camera: slow push-in with gentle handheld realism, focus pulling from berries to label.
- Overlay text: **A rich berry ritual**

Scene 2 — Engagement & Experience (3-10s)
- Show a real pour into small clear glasses, the liquid catching light with a deep ruby-burgundy glow.
- Cut to a family or couple naturally enjoying it at the table, smiling, passing a glass, and tasting it chilled.
- Include detail shots of berries, condensation on the glass, and the elegant packaging.
- Camera: macro close-up of pour, over-the-shoulder dining angle, soft side profile of hands serving.
- Overlay text 1: **99% pure Korean black raspberry**
- Overlay text 2: **Smooth, fruity, premium taste**

Scene 3 — Emotional Ending (10-15s)
- End with the bottle and carton hero shot on the table, surrounded by berries and warm ambient light, with a satisfied family-style moment in the background.
- The final shot should feel giftable, wholesome, and elevated.
- Camera: slow elegant pullback into a composed product hero frame.
- End overlay: **Berrywell Gold • 700ml**
- Optional short CTA: **Bring home the ritual**

Audio:
- NO voiceover, NO narration, NO spoken dialogue.
- Use uplifting modern cinematic music with soft premium pulses, warm ambient room tone, delicate glass clinks, and gentle pour sounds.
- Audio should end cleanly without a sting, pop, or impact hit.

Editing and pacing:
- premium rhythmic cuts, 3-5 seconds per beat, elegant transitions, no chaos
- keep product identity clear throughout
- avoid fake stock footage energy; make it feel like real captured moments from a refined wellness gathering

Negative prompt:
- no subtitles, captions, or long readable text
- no fake claims, medical promises, or unsupported health outcomes
- no distorted labels, warped bottle shape, or incorrect product design
- no scene/background/lighting/props copied from the reference image
- no extra products, random fruits, messy clutter, or unrealistic luxury styling
- no robotic hands, warped anatomy, distorted glass, morphing liquid, or inconsistent bottle appearance
- no final-second audio artifacts, impact hits, beeps, pops, or stingers

asset.mainAssetCreativeDirectionPrompt:
Create an ultra-realistic, fast-paced UGC creator POV-style 15-second product video for **BERRYWELL Black raspberry Juice (700ml)**, using the attached reference image as the source of truth for the product’s appearance. Preserve the bottle shape, dark berry liquid, label placement, cap, and any visible packaging details exactly, but do not copy the reference image’s white background, studio composition, or camera angle. Make it feel like a real person filming on their phone at home in Singapore.

Goal: sell the juice as a simple daily wellness drink with a rich berry taste and an easy routine.

Structure the video like real UGC:

1) Hook / Problem
Open with the creator looking into the phone in a kitchen or home dining area, slightly tired and relatable: they’re bored of plain drinks and want something that feels refreshing but still part of a daily routine.
- Camera: arm-length selfie framing, slight hand shake, natural indoor light.
- Spoken line: **“Okay, I was so over plain drinks every day…”**

2) Product Solution
Quick punch-in reveal of the BERRYWELL bottle on a counter, then back to the creator holding it casually.
- Show the label clearly for a second, but keep it natural and handheld.
- Spoken line: **“Then I tried this black raspberry juice from Berrywell.”**

3) Real Demo
Show a believable real-life pour: open the bottle, pour a small amount into a glass, then dilute with cold water or serve chilled over ice. Show the deep dark berry color swirling in the glass.
- Camera: handheld close-up insert, slight reframing, quick cut back to face reaction.
- Add natural ambient sounds: bottle cap twist, liquid pour, glass clink.
- Spoken line: **“You only need a little bit, and it tastes so rich.”**

4) Satisfying Result
Show the finished drink with ice on the table, creator taking a sip, then a relieved smile and small surprised reaction.
- Emphasize the refreshed mood and easy daily-use vibe, not medical claims.
- Spoken line: **“It’s actually really nice chilled — like, super easy to keep in my routine.”**

5) Reaction
Creator gives a quick honest laugh or nod, holding the glass in frame.
- Spoken line: **“Okay wait… this is kind of my new go-to.”**

6) CTA
End with creator pointing gently toward the bottle on the table, still in casual selfie POV.
- Spoken line: **“If you want a simple berry drink, go check out Berrywell.”**

Visual direction:
- self-shot creator POV, casual home environment, phone-shot realism
- slight shake, imperfect framing, quick punch-ins, fast but clear pacing
- product shown in hand, on counter, and in poured glass
- keep product accurate to the reference image across all shots
- use natural colors: deep berry reds, dark plum tones, soft kitchen neutrals
- no polished ad look, no cinematic lighting, no tripod feel

Editing and pacing:
- quick jump cuts every 1–3 seconds
- one or two punch-in zooms on the bottle and poured drink
- minimal transitions, creator-style cut rhythm
- maintain a believable real-life UGC pace

Audio:
- natural female or male creator voice, casual and unpolished
- light ambient room tone, soft TikTok-style background music low in the mix
- bottle cap twist, pour sound, ice clink, light sip sound
- voice should stay clearly audible and conversational
- end cleanly without a final sound hit

Important product details to naturally imply visually, without reading them aloud:
- 700ml bottle
- black raspberry / bokbunja juice
- premium Korean product
- daily drinking vibe
- serve chilled or diluted
- rich berry color and taste

Negative prompt:
No subtitles, captions, readable text overlays, end cards, fake social media UI, polished commercial look, cinematic shots, tripod shots, CGI, fake textures, staged acting, overproduced lighting, exaggerated enthusiasm, unsupported health or medical claims, invented certifications, invented awards, distorted bottle shape, wrong label, wrong cap, incorrect packaging, product inconsistency between shots, copied white studio background from the reference image, copied composition from the reference image, additional brand logos, third-party brand marks, warped hands, broken lip-sync, unreadable text, morphing objects, final-second boom or stinger.

styleAsset.title: Event Recap
styleAsset.goal: Cinematic recaps for events, courses, and communities.
styleAsset.selectedCreativeDirectionPrompt:
## Style Prompt

Create a cinematic, emotionally engaging 15-second recap highlight reel for digital or hybrid experiences.

This style works for webinars, Zoom sessions, online courses, virtual masterminds, creator communities, educational programs, digital memberships, challenges, virtual summits, online bootcamps, hybrid conferences, networking communities, remote creator experiences, services, businesses, and digital products.

The video should feel like a professionally edited modern recap film: cinematic, premium, modern, emotionally engaging, socially believable, and highly shareable.

It should not feel like a generic slideshow, fake stock footage, disconnected random clips, robotic webinar visuals, fake futuristic Zoom room, or traditional product ad.

The AI must first understand the promoted item:
- what the event, course, community, product, service, or business helps people achieve
- why people are attending, joining, learning, or participating
- what emotional experience participants are having
- what type of people would realistically join
- whether the experience is digital, hybrid, async, or community-based
- what virtual environment, participant density, and production scale are supported by the provided context
- what moments a real videographer would naturally capture for an online experience
- what short overlay lines can be used without inventing unsupported facts

Think: "What would a real videographer naturally capture for this digital experience?"
Do not think: "What random cinematic shots look cool?"

The recap should feel emotionally authentic, immersive, socially believable, and naturally cinematic.

### Experience Type

If the promoted item is digital, such as a webinar, Zoom session, online course, virtual summit, online bootcamp, digital community, live session, challenge, coaching call, membership, software training, or digital product, do not fake a large physical venue unless the context explicitly supports a hybrid or in-person component.

For digital experiences, show realistic remote-learning and digital-community moments: modern home setups, creator workspaces, premium laptop setups, cinematic desk scenes, webcams, monitors, headphones, coffee, notebooks, people joining online sessions, participants listening, over-the-shoulder workstation shots, typing moments, screen glow, remote collaboration, community energy, and digital creator lifestyle moments.

If the promoted item is hybrid, combine believable physical gathering moments with remote participation moments. The physical and digital sides should feel connected to the same experience.

If the promoted item is a business or service, frame the recap around customer experience, founder or team energy, community moments, service environment, participant outcome, and brand promise without inventing unsupported claims.

Participant count, location, date, duration, country count, speaker names, transformation claims, and CTA details must match the provided context. If these details are missing, keep them generic and believable instead of inventing exact numbers.

### Filming Style

The video should look like a professional cinematic digital recap shot with iPhones, webcams, mirrorless cameras, and cinematic creator setups depending on the experience type.

For digital events and online products, use:
- cinematic webcam framing
- realistic creator desk setups
- cinematic monitor glow
- over-the-shoulder workstation shots
- premium remote-work lighting
- subtle RGB or ambient reflections when they fit the brand
- elegant digital light patterns
- soft interface reflections
- abstract motion graphics around monitors when subtle and believable

The footage should feel premium, organic, polished, and realistic.

Avoid fake AI movement, robotic webcam shots, fake futuristic holograms, chaotic editing, overproduced commercial visuals, and music-video chaos.

### Digital Screen Rules

For digital events, online courses, software, dashboards, webinars, Zoom sessions, and virtual communities, do not rely on readable screen content.

Do not show readable text, dashboards, spreadsheets, Zoom interfaces, UI menus, graphs, charts, browser tabs, fake numbers, visible writing, visible notifications, stock charts, detailed presentation slides, or fake AI-generated dashboards.

Instead use:
- softly blurred screens
- abstract UI blocks
- non-readable video-call grids
- glowing interface reflections
- cinematic digital light patterns
- soft monitor glow
- elegant ambient UI shapes
- subtle digital atmosphere
- participants reacting to screens
- cursor movement or scrolling without readable content

Screens should feel cinematic, believable, modern, and premium without relying on readable content.

### Environment Generation

Generate realistic environments based on whether the experience is digital or hybrid.

Digital examples:
- webinars in modern home setups
- online courses in creator workspaces
- virtual masterminds in cinematic desk setups
- remote communities in cozy creator environments
- online bootcamps in premium laptop setups
- live sessions in cinematic streaming spaces
- coaching calls in modern minimal home offices

Hybrid examples:
- small in-person host spaces connected to remote audiences
- coworking spaces with livestream setups
- studio rooms with cameras, monitors, and a remote community
- physical workshop rooms with remote participants visible only as non-readable screen grids

The environment should feel lived-in, authentic, premium but believable, socially active, and visually aesthetic.

Include details that fit the experience:
- laptops
- webcams
- monitors
- headphones
- coffee
- notebooks
- realistic desk setups
- lighting setups
- subtle environmental movement
- believable creator spaces
- ambient digital glow
- crowd movement or room energy when relevant

Computer screens must remain blurred, abstract, non-readable, and cinematic.

Avoid empty spaces, fake luxury, unrealistic futuristic environments, cluttered compositions, readable screens, fake holographic dashboards, visible UI text, and physical event scenes that conflict with an online-only product.

### People And Participants

Generate realistic attendees, speakers, hosts, instructors, creators, moderators, students, customers, founders, team members, and participants who naturally fit the category.

People should feel authentic, expressive, collaborative, socially natural, emotionally believable, relaxed but energized.

Use natural body language, realistic eye movement, subtle smiles, believable reactions, casual interactions, genuine community moments, note-taking, laptop work, typing, screen listening, and realistic online participation.

Avoid robotic participants, staged acting, awkward posing, exaggerated reactions, fake business stock-photo energy, and random people who do not match the audience.

### Scene Generation Rules

Generate cinematic recap moments that logically connect like a real digital recap film.

Digital event shots may include:
- people joining online sessions
- cinematic desk setups
- creators listening to workshops
- over-the-shoulder workstation shots
- cinematic monitor glow
- webcam participation
- typing moments
- remote collaboration
- learning environments
- digital creator lifestyle moments
- subtle digital atmosphere around monitors

Hybrid shots may include:
- physical host or speaker setup
- small group workshop activity
- livestream production details
- remote attendees reacting through abstract screen grids
- connected physical and digital community moments

Every shot should connect to the promoted item and experience. Do not create random disconnected clips.

### Dynamic Text Overlay System

This style intentionally uses controlled premium text overlays as part of the recap format.

Distribute short cinematic one-line overlays naturally throughout the video. Use only a few high-impact lines, not subtitles or captions.

The AI should generate overlay lines based on:
- what the event, course, community, product, service, or business is
- whether it is digital or hybrid
- where it is happening if known
- attendee or community energy
- what people are learning
- networking, transformation, collaboration, creator culture, or digital participation

Overlay text should feel cinematic, premium, minimal, emotionally engaging, highly readable, and naturally integrated. Use elegant typography, clean spacing, smooth fade animations, cinematic placement, and subtle motion graphics.

Do not invent exact attendee counts, country counts, dates, cities, ratings, speaker names, revenue claims, or outcomes unless provided in the context. If specific information is missing, use generic but useful copy such as the event name, category, audience, learning theme, community energy, digital participation, or CTA.

The final scene may end with the product, event, course, community, or business name and a clean CTA generated from the context. The CTA should be short, natural, and commercially useful without sounding aggressive.

Avoid aggressive advertisements, cheap popups, cluttered captions, meme text, long paragraphs, tiny text, unreadable UI copy, fake UI, and subtitle-style dialogue.

### Editing And Pacing

The final video should feel like a premium modern recap film.

Use rhythmic editing synced to music, cinematic transitions, emotional build-up, engaging progression, smooth pacing, premium momentum, and a clear beginning, middle, and ending.

The pacing should feel uplifting, immersive, exciting, and modern.

Avoid glitchy transitions, hyper-fast cuts, chaotic editing, random camera changes, and music-video chaos.

### Audio

No voiceovers.
No dialogue.
No narration.
No talking-to-camera.
No subtitles.
No captions.

Use only:
- cinematic upbeat background music
- modern electronic, inspirational, or community-driven music
- subtle event ambience
- crowd atmosphere
- keyboard clicks
- room tone
- typing sounds
- digital ambience
- environmental audio
- applause when relevant

The soundtrack should feel uplifting, future-forward, emotionally engaging, and community-driven. It should end cleanly without abrupt final-second pops, thuds, beeps, or impact hits.

### Visual Style

Use cinematic event aesthetics, premium modern color grading, realistic skin textures, clean compositions, authentic lighting, realistic reflections, natural motion blur, shallow depth of field, realistic monitor glow, premium social-media framing, and subtle digital atmosphere when relevant.

The final result should feel like a viral premium event, course, community, or digital-experience recap video.

### 15-Second Structure

Scene 1 - Opening Atmosphere (0-3s)
Establish the physical venue, digital environment, community setting, learning space, or hybrid context. Show attendee energy, setup moments, ambient movement, screen glow, room atmosphere, people arriving, or participants joining.

Display one short cinematic overlay introducing the experience, location or digital setting if known, event type, audience, or community energy.

Scene 2 - Engagement And Experience (3-10s)
Show the most important participation moments: networking, collaboration, learning, teaching, discussion, reactions, creator activity, digital engagement, physical engagement, community energy, remote work, note-taking, screen interaction, or immersive moments.

Distribute one or two premium one-line overlays naturally through this sequence. Keep the overlays short and factually supported.

Scene 3 - Emotional Ending (10-15s)
End with applause, smiles, final networking visuals, digital connection moments, participant satisfaction, celebratory atmosphere, cinematic closing visuals, or a polished brand moment.

The final shot should reveal the promoted item name or brand identity with a short CTA when appropriate. End on an aspirational, credible, human emotional note.

### Negative Prompt

Avoid: voiceovers, narration, spoken dialogue, subtitles, captions, fake stock footage, random disconnected shots, readable computer screens, visible UI text, spreadsheets, stock charts, fake Zoom interfaces, robotic webcam behavior, fake futuristic holograms, unsupported attendee counts, invented dates, invented locations, invented country counts, invented speaker names, fake transformation claims, fake physical venues for online-only products, glitch effects, warped anatomy, distorted faces, unrealistic camera movement, robotic participants, fake networking interactions, stiff body language, chaotic editing, cluttered compositions, unrealistic environments, floating objects, awkward crowd behavior, aggressive transitions, overproduced commercial energy, music-video chaos, unreadable small text, long text overlays, fake app UI, distorted logos, hallucinated branding.
